label: money, price and paying
note: Chapter 91. The note was right that no word for money, price, buying or selling appeared anywhere, and right that it blocked the whole shopping scenario. It closes together with ML-A1-LEX-31 because the two are one situation. WHAT MADE IT CHEAP WAS CHAPTER 88. The price question is ethra roopa, and ethra was lifted out of the age question in chapter 81, so the question is two words of which one was already owned. The ANSWER is the part that had been impossible: before the tens were taught, the count stopped at twenty and every price above it was unsayable -- which is exactly what ML-A1-NUM-04's note had warned. So this chapter only had to name the unit being counted. vila and panam are the price and the money; panam ends in -am, which tells the learner in advance how it will behave when A CASE ENDING attaches. (Narrowed under HL-C400.) vaanguka (to buy) is built on the -uka ending the verbs already use, and its object stays BARE -- pustakam takes no object ending because it is a thing and not a person, which is chapter 87's rule holding while the verb changed. Verified before writing: panam, vila, kada, roopa and vaanguka ALL returned ZERO files.
